identity_evidence.quote: A 28-year-old male presented with a history of headache since 2 months

attribution_limitations: The abstract gives the age as 26-year-old whereas the case report text gives 28-year-old for the same patient. Both age facts are kept review-only; no age is chosen.
The discussion says unnoticed trauma might have been the possible cause of the tuberculosis; this is a hedged author suggestion, not an asserted cause, and no trauma history is documented.

The abstract and introduction describe the case as primary calvarial tuberculosis with no tuberculosis elsewhere, but only a chest x-ray is documented as the search for another focus; the article does not describe a wider workup. Pus culture result is not reported.
The text cites Figure 3 for the CT done on follow up after 1 month, but the Figure 3 caption itself states no time; its findings are kept untimed and are not attached to the 1-month CT event.
The pericranium is the only specimen named as sent for histopathology, but the result sentence names no specimen and reports bony fragments; the specimen is not attached to the result.
The completed "course of therapy" is not named in its sentence; the abstract places the patient doing well after anti-tubercular therapy.
